findings.reason: REST client TLS hostname verification is explicitly disabled here, so the client will not verify the peer hostname against the server certificate.
findings.fix: Remove the null override and let endpoint identification remain enabled for REST clients, or set the appropriate HTTPS hostname verification algorithm only when a vetted exception is required.

findings.reason: This logs the raw AWS secret access key value, which is sensitive credential material.
findings.fix: Do not log the secret key value; remove the message or replace it with a non-sensitive constant such as a presence/length indicator.

findings.reason: This logs the keystore password in cleartext at info level, exposing a secret used to load private-key material.
findings.fix: Remove this log line or replace it with a redacted placeholder; never emit the password itself.

findings.reason: This logs the AWS session token value, which is a live credential secret.
findings.fix: Delete the log statement or log only a constant/status message without the token value.

verificationSteps: Search the four files for any remaining logs that interpolate secret material (passwords, secret keys, session tokens) and confirm only redacted/status-only logging remains.
Run a unit test or targeted static check that exercises S3 delegation token init/receive paths and assert log output never contains the configured secret key, keystore password, or session token.
Create a REST client SSL context from SSLUtils and confirm the resulting Netty SSL context no longer disables endpoint identification; verify the peer hostname is checked during TLS handshake.
Re-run existing REST-over-TLS connection tests against a certificate whose SAN/CN does not match the host and confirm the client now fails hostname verification.
uncertainties: I did not inspect call sites or deployment settings, so I cannot determine whether the REST TLS hostname check is additionally overridden elsewhere.
The access-key-ID log lines were not treated as leaks because access-key IDs are not secret keys on their own.
